sourceInformation.genre: Surgical action game, with story scenes and a small walkable ward
sourceInformation.perspective: First-person top-down on the operative field; front-on portrait stages for story; three-quarter view for the ward; side view for the title
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge v0.89.1 (handoff package; one engine patch: the touch notice), AI Hub session client (vendor/hub/session.js, Session Protocol v1; client version unknown), plain JavaScript, Web Audio, Playwright 1.63 for browser tests
sourceInformation.artDirection: The engine's pixel look at PS1 level: per-pixel wet tissue through hand-picked ramps with ordered dithering, flat-shaded bust portraits, painted story stages, all by code; the engine's props for the ward
sourceInformation.animation: The engine's Humanoid rigs for the ward; continuous-value procedural animation for organs, parasites, instruments and portraits (blink, bob, mouth flap)
sourceInformation.audio: All in code on Web Audio: synthesized effects, a parasite choir, Animalese-style gibberish voices, songs in the engine's notation with music at 10% by default
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1, shared world, 1 to 4 players (Grand Rounds); couch co-op with AI colleagues on its own
sourceInformation.testing: Headless scripts in Node that play the game and check state, including a scripted playthrough of the whole game; Playwright browser checks, the Hub harness and screenshots only for what scripts cannot check; no subagents or workflows used to review
sourceInformation.research: Read the plan (which summarizes Wikipedia and Marc Normandin's Retro XP essay on the source), the engine's API card and the Hub protocol page; no other research

testingFeedback: 14 issues were logged by tests (and 3 more layout problems by screenshots).

9 were game breaking: incisions that never closed a phase, a magnet fighting the guide-follow, a wire-order check that was always wrong, unreachable slur marks, a crash from a name collision, an untargetable spiral, a Last Note that never held, a stale story flag, and a stale scene flag.
The bot playing every case through the real cursor path at Resident with cheats off: it found most of the real bugs and set the balance numbers.
Screenshot sweeps: they only found layout overlaps, never sim bugs.
engineFeedback: The pixel look, rigs, standard menus and settings for free, and headless advance with a stand-in canvas that ran the whole game in Node.
Yes: scene objects are shared across visits so stale state carried over twice; I also guessed wrong about where a held object's per-step hook runs.
The operation sim, the cursor with assist, the tissue sites and strains, the bot, the Hub mirror, busts, stages, music, voices and the choir.
Keeping three views (overhead field, front-on stage, three-quarter ward) in one look and one input scheme.
Only the touch notice string: the notice now sits at the bottom so the attract reel shows above it, and the Settings button takes taps.
A per-system time scale: Long Breath needs the world slowed while the hands stay at full speed, and the engine's timeScale is global.
promptFeedback: A complete plan with verified facts, exact numbers, an originality rule and a done checklist.
The scope: eleven distinct operations, a story, a Hub protocol, attract, dev mode and tests for one agent in one run; the plan's own cut list helped.
Making every strain a distinct, fair mechanic that a bot can also beat.
Mark earlier which tests need a browser and trim the content list so polish gets budget.

aiHub.name: Sutures & Sorrows
aiHub.description: A rookie surgeon and a deadpan nurse race to save patients from a parasite that sings, in a hospital soap opera played with eight surgical tools. Alone, on one couch, or with up to four surgeons in a Hub session.
aiHub.controls: Aim: right stick or mouse. Use tool: R2 or click. Pick tool: left stick or 1-8. Gift: Triangle or F
